transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to shake this heavy feeling. It's like... I don't know, like everything I've tried to build since my divorce just fell apart, and I'm just sort of... stuck under it. It's just very hopeless.
Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way since your divorce—days, weeks, months, or longer?
Um... about a month, I guess. It just... it really settled in when all the financial mess from the divorce started.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy since this started?
I don't know... I guess so. I just haven't really felt like doing much of anything lately.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Um... yeah. It's been bad. I just... I lie there for hours. Staring at the ceiling. Thinking about the bills, or... things I messed up at work. And if I do sleep, I end up waking up way before the sun's even out. It just... feels like I didn't sleep at all.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of feeling this down, hopeless, or unmotivated—at any earlier point in your life, even before the divorce?
Um... no. I don't think so. Not... not like this, anyway. I don't really remember.
Do you feel this heavy, hopeless mood throughout the day regardless of what you're doing, or does it mainly come up when you're thinking about the divorce and its aftermath?

It's... pretty much all day. It doesn't really matter what I'm doing. I just... I can't shake it. 

This heavy... hopeless feeling. It's just like... everything I tried to build after the divorce just collapsed. And I'm just... sitting under it. That's why I came in, I guess.
Have you noticed feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about things, or trouble concentrating, that go beyond just worrying about the divorce and its aftermath?

I... yeah, I guess. I just... I think a lot about how bad I am at... everything. 

Like... I'll just sit there and think about how I'm a terrible engineer. Or how I failed at being a wife. And I just... I replay every little mistake. Every calculation I messed up, or... some email I sent that sounded wrong. It just feels like proof that I... I just ruin things. I don't know. It's hard to focus on anything else.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or wishing you weren't alive during this time?

I... um... yeah. I guess. 

Just... thinking that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. It got... kind of intense recently. I think I scared myself a bit. That's... that's actually why I called the employee assistance program at work.
Have you thought about a specific way you might end your life, or made any plans to act on these thoughts?
No. Um... no, I haven't. I don't... I don't have a plan or anything. Just... just what I said before.
